To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the number of tweets per capita is strongly correlated with the number of Internet users per capita, and with the GDP per capita, (ii) the number of Twitter users per capita is strongly positively correlated with the GDP per person and the number of Internet connections per capita, and (iii) the number of followers per user is strongly positively correlated to the GDP per person, the Internet connections per capita and the number of tweets.
the most active country is the US, followed by the UK, and that the least active is China, followed by India, and that countries are similar in many ways but different in others.

1) the most active country is the US; 2) Twitter users are mostly positive, but there are significant differences in sentiment across countries; 3) the most popular languages are English and Spanish; 4) the US and Spain have the most active users; 5) there are significant differences across countries in terms of the number of followers and friends; and 6) there is a significant difference across countries in terms network topology.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Twitter is not a homogeneous platform, and that the way people use it is strongly influenced by their country of origin.

(1) Twitter is used differently in each country, but there are also some similarities, e.g., in the use of languages, the number of tweets, or the use of hashtags; (2) there is a correlation between the size of the population of each country and the number of tweets; (3) there is no clear correlation between the number of tweets and the number of users in each country.
Twitter users are very similar in many aspects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in spite of some differences, there is more commonality in the way Twitter is used than one might think.
, although there are some differences in how people use Twitter, the overall behavior and characteristics are similar for all countries.

, while Twitter usage is very similar across the countries we studied, there are some differences in activity, sentiment and use of languages, as well as in network structure, that are worth exploring.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there are significant differences between countries, and that these differences are consistent across all the metrics we analyzed, which suggests that they may be related to cultural and social aspects.
, despite the global reach of social media, there is a clear distinction between countries, which can be explained by cultural, political, and economic factors.
, despite some similarities between countries, the way social media is used differs significantly across the world.
